title: Performance Skate Sharpening Service
shortDescription: Clean, consistent skate sharpening for hockey, goalie, and figure skates.
description: A proper sharpening restores clean edges and helps the skate hold through stops, crossovers, turns, and pushes. Penguin staff can help choose a hollow based on player weight, ice conditions, skating level, and whether the skater wants more bite or more glide.
altText: Performance Skate Sharpening Service service bench image for Penguin Skate proof-of-concept storefront.

specifications.Best for: Routine edge maintenance before games, practices, tests, and public skating.
specifications.Typical timing: Same-day timing may vary with shop volume.
specifications.Coach note: Ask for more bite if you slide out on tight turns; ask for more glide if the skate feels stuck in the ice.
specifications.What to bring: Both skates and your preferred hollow if you already know it.
specifications.Store note: Service details and timing are confirmed by Penguin staff at drop-off.

title: Blade Mounting & Holder Alignment Service
shortDescription: Mounting and alignment support for figure blades, hockey holders, and replacement steel setups.
description: Accurate blade or holder alignment matters for balance, edge control, and confidence. This service is for new figure blades, replacement hockey holders, loose mounting hardware, or skaters who feel like one skate tracks differently than the other.
altText: Blade Mounting & Holder Alignment Service service bench image for Penguin Skate proof-of-concept storefront.

specifications.Best for: New blade installs, holder replacement, alignment checks, and loose hardware concerns.
specifications.Typical timing: Confirmed after inspection at the service counter.
specifications.Coach note: Uneven tracking can show up as trouble holding an inside or outside edge on one side.
specifications.What to bring: Boots, blades or holders, mounting hardware if supplied, and any coach or fitter notes.
specifications.Store note: Service details and timing are confirmed by Penguin staff at drop-off.

title: Skate Heat Molding Service
shortDescription: Heat molding support to help compatible skate boots wrap more comfortably around the foot.
description: Heat molding can improve initial comfort and heel lock on compatible hockey and figure boots. Penguin staff will confirm that the skate model is heat moldable, warm the boot appropriately, and help the skater seat the heel and lace the boot correctly while it sets.

specifications.Best for: New compatible skates, heel lock improvements, and break-in comfort.
specifications.Typical timing: Usually handled during a fitting visit when the bench is available.

title: Boot Punch & Fit Adjustment Service
shortDescription: Targeted skate boot adjustments for pressure points, bunions, ankle rub, and fit hot spots.
description: A boot punch or stretch can relieve specific pressure areas without changing the entire fit of the skate. This service is best after identifying an exact hot spot, such as a bunion, navicular pressure, ankle bone rub, or toe-box irritation.

specifications.Best for: Localized pressure points after the skate size and model have already been confirmed.
specifications.Typical timing: Confirmed after staff inspect the boot material and pressure area.

specifications.What to bring: Both skates, skating socks, and a clear description of where pressure appears.

title: Rivet & Eyelet Repair Service
shortDescription: Repair for loose rivets, missing eyelets, and boot hardware that affects skate safety and support.
description: Loose rivets, damaged eyelets, or worn mounting hardware can make a skate feel unstable and can get worse quickly under game pressure. Penguin staff can inspect the boot, identify the affected hardware, and recommend a repair before the skate goes back on the ice.

specifications.Best for: Loose holders, missing rivets, pulled eyelets, and hardware checks.

specifications.What to bring: Both skates and any loose hardware or steel that came off the boot.

description: Not every skate problem is obvious from the bench or the ice. This inspection gives staff a chance to look at the boot, blade, holder, rivets, runner condition, and fit concern before recommending sharpening, repair, replacement parts, or a fitter consultation.

title: CCM RIBCOR 90K Senior Hockey Skates
shortDescription: CCM RIBCOR 90K Senior Hockey Skates adds a researched hockey skates option to the Penguin Skate concept catalog, with multiple images and shopper-friendly merchandising details.
description: TheCCM RIBCOR 90K SR Hockey Skates are a performance elite level skate one step down from the top of the line 100k Pro skates. The 90k offers many of the same features and performance attributes in a more affordable package. Some key features to look out for in the new 90k is the 3D Lasted 2-Piece Flexframe boot, Asymmetrical XS Dual Layer Tongue, and XS 1 Stainless (+2mm) steel. Skate Fit Profile CCM has followed suit within the industry and made their skates more accessible to different foot shapes and profiles. Like the 100k Pro, the 90k will be stepping away from D, EE widths, and be using regular, and wide fit profiles. The new fit system is a result of the most common shapes amongst the 3D Scan system CCM introduced a couple of years ago. Boot Construction & Stiffness Profile The quarter package on the CCM 90k features Flexframe technology. This technology is infused into the RFM Composite boot which is an NHL-Caliber lightweight composite material. This 3D ergonomic boot provides excellent comfort and enhances forward flexion and lateral stability to maximize your stride. The Ribcore boot will continue to have a softer stiffness level amongst CCM families. This promotes quick movements and increases range of motion to maximize your overall agility on the ice. CCM’s stiffness performance index indicates the 90k has a 165 variable index. This index allows the flexible core of the boot to enhance your biomechanics with every stride. This, paired with a new flexible tendon guard will give you an unmatched feeling of comfort and the ability to move deeply into your strides and sharp turns. Liner & Internal Padding The liner in the Ribcore 90k is the TotalDri comfort. This high performance liner is moisture-wicking which keeps your feet dry and your skates light. The liner also helps in the post-skate drying stage to help the boots be ready for the next time they’re put on. This is great for tournaments and next day ice times when the turnaround time is fast. The internal padding features an adapted memory foam to provide a comfortable wrap around the fit and to optimize the comfort of the skate. The injected smooth contour pro pad at the top of the boot provides additional comfort in a potential high pressure point area when games are getting intense. Tongue Another key upgrade new to the CCM Ribcore 90k is the Replaceable Asymmetrical Dual Layer tongue. It consists of 7mm felt, with reinforcement layers for increased comfort and protection. However, the tongues are interchangeable on the new Ribcore 90k skates to allow a more customized fit and protection level. The available replacement options, or custom options are the Pro tongue with 10mm black felt, and the Lightweight 4mm tongue. Insoles The CCM Ortholite footbed in the 90k is a lightweight insole to provide maximum comfort and support for your arches. Lacing System The Ribcore line continues with the standard eyelet lacing system. The top eyelets are also reinforced for increased durability. Steel Runner, Holder & Blade Profile For the Ribcore 90k, the stock steel will be the XS 1 Stainless Steel. This blade provides a long-lasting edge for long-term performance. Furthermore, it is 12% taller in height than standard blades for better turns. The CCM Speedblade XS is mounted on the 90k skates, offering the sturdy quick release system that has become a staple amongst the top end players around the world. Graphics The new graphic for the CCM Ribcore line features a sleek black finish with chrome accents and logo along the base of the boot. A fine line of classic Ribcore green pulls everything together down the middle.

The top of the boot is lined with Comfort Edge Padding to reduce bite when performing stops and aggressive tight turns. The tongue includes a 40 oz Pro Stock felt tongue infused with an injected comfort pad down the middle to offer a balance of performance, support, and great feel. Steel Runner, Holder & Blade Profile The X Velocity skate is equipped with Tuuk Lightspeed 1+ Black steel. shortDescription: Buttendz Goal Sentry Butt-End Tape Grip expands the Penguin Skate accessories assortment with a practical add-on item, multiple product images, and clear shopper-ready details.
description: Intro & New Features Designed in collaboration with LA Kings Jonathan Quick, The Buttendz Goal Sentry Butt-End Tape Grip is the ultimate goalie grip. With an over-sized knob and tiling all around the handle, the grip provides everything a tendy needs to protect their net. Reasons to Switch to Buttendz Grip Tape 1. Improves the feel of the puck: The elasticity of the natural rubber in buttendz handles helps absorbed the energy transfer from the puck to your stick, this makes it easier to control. 2. Helps with shot power and accuracy: The tackiness of the buttendz handles allows you to have optimal wrist movement and flexibility due to the reduced tension and strength needed to hold your stick allowing for a smoother more powerful accurate shot. 3. Increase the life of your gloves: Regular hockey tape has a cloth side and an adhesive side. After constant use on a tape job the cloth side wears off and your gloves are now exposed to the chemicals that were on the adhesive side. With constant friction and the combination of the chemicals, the palm of the gloves begins to wear out. Buttendz eliminates both these problems. How to Apply Buttendz Grip Tape Each Buttendz comes with an application spray with enough in each bottle to do multiply applications. 1. Coat the entire inside of the buttendz grip with the application spray (about 10 sprays) 2. Press the grip flat on itself so the sides are touching to help spread the application spray. 3. Take your stick and coat where you are going to put the grip with the application spray, make sure there are no dry areas. 4. Start on a corner of your stick and push the grip over the edge until it’s on the top of your stick. Once on twist down until the top of your stick and the grip are level with each other, do not go too low or leave too high. Let sit for at least an hour before using, overnight is best. Or 5. Take two hands and grab the inside of the bottom of the grip and pull over the end of the stick. Once on the stick twist the stick and the grip in opposite directions while pulling the grip down at the same time. Stop once the top of your stick and the grip are level with each other, do not go too low or leave too high. Let sit for at least an hour before using, overnight is best. How to Take Off Buttendz Grip Tape Break a twig or got a new one, but still want to use your Buttendz grip? No problem! Buttendz grips are reusable and here is the best way to remove it from your stick. 1. Use hand soap or dish soap. Take the back of a spoon and slide it gently under the grip to allow a gap. Pour a little bit of soap into the gap. Repeat this on all four sides of the grip and on the top and bottom. 2. Gently start to twist. The grip will begin to loosen. Once loose enough, twist stick and grip in opposite directions while pulling the grip off the stick. 3. Once the grip Is off, clean the entire inside of the grip by rinsing thoroughly with water to get all the soap off. Allow to completely dry before reusing.
